title: Ramayana to release in nearly 40 languages worldwide; Namit Malhotra and team mount an unprecedented overseas release
raw_summary:
Less than a month is left for the release of Ramayana, and the excitement is steadily building. Yesterday, the makers finally announced that the much-awaited film will release in cinemas worldwide on November 5. They also revealed that advance bookings will commence on Dussehra, October 20. Meanwhile, the makers are working round the clock to ensure an unprecedented release in overseas markets.

A trade source told Bollywood Hungama, “Producer Namit Malhotra and the core team of Ramayana are determined to make it the biggest release ever for an Indian film. They have been working towards this goal for a long time. The film's promotion at CinemaCon 2026 and San Diego Comic-Con was a step in that direction. Getting Sony Pictures on board for international distribution was also a huge shot in the arm.”

The source continued, “To make the film accessible and appealing to audiences across the globe, Ramayana has been dubbed in nearly 40 languages. As a result, viewers across the world will be able to experience the film in all its glory in a language they understand, without having to rely on subtitles. This is the first time an Indian film has been dubbed on such a massive scale. The complete list of languages in which the film has been dubbed will be unveiled in a week or two.”

Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. It is directed by Nitesh Tiwari of Dangal (2016) fame and produced by Namit Malhotra. The music is composed by A R Rahman and Hans Zimmer.

The mythological epic is being made as a two-part saga, with the first instalment arriving in cinemas on November 5, 2026, that is, in the Diwali week. The second part is scheduled for release during Diwali 2027.

title: FIR register against Imran Khan and others over August Kranti Maidan protest: REPORT
raw_summary:
Mumbai Police have registered a First Information Report (FIR) against actor Imran Khan, his girlfriend Lekha Washington and several others following their detention during a protest at August Kranti Maidan on Saturday, October 10. The demonstration was organised in support of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest in Delhi, which called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The FIR was registered at Gamdevi police station under Sections 223, 126(2), 189(2), 189(3) and 189(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), according to reports. The provisions cited in the case relate to disobedience of orders issued by public servants, wrongful restraint and offences associated with unlawful assembly. The complaint was filed by police personnel following the gathering, which took place amid heightened security arrangements in the area.

According to reports, more than 400 people were detained during the protest, with some accounts putting the number at around 600 across Mumbai. Those detained included Imran, Lekha and Imran’s cousin, Zayn Marie Khan. They were released later that night.

Ahead of the demonstration, police personnel had barricaded roads surrounding August Kranti Maidan and deployed additional staff to prevent the gathering from proceeding. The detentions took place as authorities maintained security in the area.

Following his detention, Imran took to Instagram to share a selfie from inside a police van. The actor accompanied the picture with the caption, “Apparently I'm going for a drive.”

Lekha also shared updates on social media following the detention. She said she did not know where the police were taking them. After their release, she alleged that the police were not allowing them to return home or arrange a vehicle. She later reassured her followers that they were safe and on their way home.

The Mumbai protest was held in solidarity with the CJP’s demonstration in Delhi, where protesters were also detained during a major police operation. The movement has been demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over allegations concerning the revision of electoral rolls.

With the registration of the FIR, the legal proceedings against Imran, Lekha and the other individuals named in the case have become a fresh development following Saturday’s demonstration. Further details about the case and any subsequent police action remain awaited.

title: Ajay Devgn begins shooting for Chauhaan in Kargil; returns to Ladakh 23 years after LOC: Kargil

Ajay Devgn delivered a blockbuster this year with Drishyam The Conclusion, which was released during the lucrative October 2 weekend. Interestingly, the actor is gearing up for another release around the same period next year, Chauhaan. Bollywood Hungama has learned that Ajay recently began shooting for the war drama in Kargil, Ladakh.

A source from Ladakh told Bollywood Hungama, “Ajay Devgn is shooting for Chauhaan in Kargil. He arrived here a few days ago and has already begun filming. Some key scenes will be shot in this picturesque town. The makers had obtained the necessary permissions in advance and have made elaborate arrangements to ensure that the shoot goes smoothly.”

The source continued, “It’s quite cold here in Kargil, and the weather will surely add an authentic touch to the scenes of Chauhaan.”

Interestingly, this is not the first time Ajay Devgn is shooting in Ladakh. He had earlier filmed some crucial scenes for J P Dutta’s war film LOC: Kargil (2003) in the mountainous region. At that time, Ladakh was part of the erstwhile state of Jammu & Kashmir. It became a separate Union Territory in 2019, with Leh and Kargil as its two capitals.

Chauhaan is directed by Neeraj Yadav and produced by Jyoti Deshpande, Aanand L Rai and Himanshu Sharma under Jio Studios and Colour Yellow Productions. The film was announced on June 25, 2026, on the birth anniversary of the late action director Veeru Devgan, Ajay Devgn’s father. It is scheduled to release in cinemas on October 1, 2027.

The announcement video featured the song ‘Jumma Chumma De De’ playing in the background and ended with the dialogue, “Pathaanon se kehna, Chauhaan aa raha hai.” The film marks Ajay Devgn’s first collaboration with filmmaker Aanand L Rai. Jio Studios serves as both presenter and producer on the project.

title: Ranveer Singh brings home a Rs. 1.95 crore electric luxury sedan; all you need to know about his BMW i7
raw_summary:
Bollywood star Ranveer Singh has added a new luxury car to his garage, with the actor taking delivery of the BMW i7 50 xDrive, the all-electric version of the German automaker’s flagship 7 Series sedan. The luxury electric car is priced at Rs. 1.95 crore (ex-showroom), making it a significant addition to the actor’s already impressive collection of automobiles.

The acquisition comes shortly after Ranveer was unveiled as BMW India’s brand ambassador and introduced the company’s latest 7 Series range at a launch event in New Delhi in September. The actor’s association with the brand now gets an interesting personal touch, with the star bringing home one of its flagship electric offerings.

The BMW i7 50 xDrive M Sport combines the presence and comfort expected from a flagship luxury sedan with the benefits of an all-electric powertrain. The model produces 455 hp and 600 Nm of torque, with a claimed 0-100 kmph acceleration time of 5.5 seconds. It features a 112.5 kWh battery pack and offers a claimed driving range of up to 728 km on the WLTP cycle.

The car also places considerable emphasis on passenger comfort and in-cabin technology. Its features include a large rear-seat entertainment screen, a premium Bowers & Wilkins sound system, executive lounge seating and an upgraded infotainment setup. The new i7 is locally manufactured at BMW Group’s Chennai facility, making India the only country outside Germany to produce the electric flagship.

For Ranveer, whose larger-than-life personality often extends to his automobile choices, the i7 represents a move towards electric luxury without compromising on performance or road presence. title: Hanuman Ansh, Cocktail 2 create tourism BOOM: Kainchi Dham witnesses MASSIVE crowds; Italy bookings jump 38%
raw_summary:
Films have often influenced the travel plans of moviegoers, inspiring them to visit destinations they have admired on the big screen. Switzerland became a dream destination for many Indians after its picturesque locations were showcased in Yash Chopra's films. Kaho Naa Pyaar Hai (2000) encouraged viewers to explore New Zealand, while Spain found a place on travellers' wish lists after Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011). Similarly, 3 Idiots (2009) made Ladakh's Pangong Lake a must-visit destination. In recent times, two films have once again demonstrated the power of cinema in boosting tourism – Hanuman Ansh and Cocktail 2.

Last weekend, videos and pictures emerged of tourists and devotees thronging Kainchi Dham near Nainital, Uttarakhand. The surge in footfalls has been partly attributed to the sleeper blockbuster Hanuman Ansh, which is based on the life of Neeb Karori Baba, whose ashram is situated at Kainchi Dham.

A recent report in Bombay Times, published before the October 2 weekend rush, quoted Sanjeev Kumar, General Manager, Naukuchia House, Naukuchiatal – IHCL SeleQtions, as saying, “The interest around Hanuman Ansh, Neem Karoli Baba and Kainchi Dham has renewed attention on the spiritual landscape of Kumaon. Film-led interest can encourage travellers to look beyond the screen and discover the local culture, faith, food, people and landscape. That is when storytelling becomes meaningful for a destination – when a film sparks curiosity and leads to a more personal journey.”

However, the sudden popularity has also brought its share of problems. ThePrint published a detailed report on how locals are struggling to cope with the influx of tourists in the post-Hanuman Ansh era. The report revealed that rooms which normally cost Rs. 2,000-3,000 per night were being offered for as much as Rs. 7,000 during the recent rush. The massive crowds also led to traffic congestion and put pressure on local infrastructure.

This is also an example of the flip side of film tourism, where a destination becomes so popular that it struggles to accommodate the influx of visitors. The situation has prompted authorities to consider stricter measures. According to reports, the administration is planning to introduce a registration system for visitors, initially on weekends, to regulate the crowds and ensure a smoother experience for devotees.

On the other hand, Italy has once again caught the imagination of Indian moviegoers, and the credit partly goes to Cocktail 2, starring Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon and Rashmika Mandanna. A significant portion of the film's first half is set in picturesque Italian locations such as Catania, Noto, Siracusa, Castellammare del Golfo, Avola and Milan. These places have been beautifully captured on the big screen, giving viewers yet another reason to consider Italy for their next holiday.

According to the Bombay Times report, Aloke Bajpai, Group CEO, ixigo, revealed, “Since Cocktail 2 was released, bookings on our site to and from Italy are up 38% YoY.”

He further stated, “According to Great Indian Travel Index report, released last year, YoY bookings on ixigo to cities across the Northeast grew sharply, Dimapur +77%, Agartala +48%, and Guwahati and Imphal +44% each, with shows like The Family Man helping bring these destinations into the spotlight. We are seeing the same internationally. Sicily, featured in The White Lotus, The Odyssey and Cocktail 2, is a great example.”

The developments once again underline the influence of cinema beyond the box office. While films can introduce audiences to destinations they may never have considered visiting, the growing popularity of these places also raises questions about whether local infrastructure is equipped to handle the sudden influx. Hanuman Ansh and Cocktail 2 are two contrasting examples of this phenomenon, showing how the magic of the movies can translate into real-world travel, economic opportunities and, at times, unexpected challenges.

title: Ramesh Taurani recalls Alka Yagnik’s rise in the ’90s: “She was getting the most songs”
raw_summary:
Producer Ramesh Taurani recently reflected on the changing dynamics of Hindi film music in the 1990s and recalled how Alka Yagnik emerged as one of the most sought-after female playback singers of the decade. Taurani was speaking alongside his brother Kumar Taurani on Komal Nahta’s Game Changers: The Music Series.

Discussing the music landscape of the period, Ramesh Taurani recalled that established voices such as Lata Mangeshkar and Asha Bhosle continued to be important choices for filmmakers, while a new generation of singers was gaining prominence.

“Back then, Lata Ji and Asha Ji were already established. When we used to make music, Lata Ji was our first preference, followed by Alka and Anuradha,” Taurani said.

He went on to recall the emergence of singers including Kumar Sanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan. According to him, films such as Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, Aashiqui, Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante helped establish the new voices in the industry as their songs became popular with audiences.

“The idea was that in the ’90s, when new singers like Shanu, Anuradha Paudwal, Alka Yagnik and Udit Narayan came in, these four made it big. Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak, Aashiqui, Saajan and Phool Aur Kaante were hits, and their songs became superhits,” he recalled. How Alka Yagnik emerged as a leading female voice Taurani also drew a comparison between the newer singers and the established female playback voices of the previous generation. He recalled that Anuradha Paudwal was being viewed as a successor to Lata Mangeshkar, while Alka Yagnik was increasingly being positioned as a voice comparable to Asha Bhosle.

“The idea then was that Anuradha Paudwal was the new Lata Mangeshkar, while Alka Yagnik became the new Asha Bhosle,” Taurani said.

According to Taurani, the shift in Anuradha Paudwal’s film career eventually created more opportunities for Alka Yagnik. He recalled that after Paudwal stopped singing for films and became associated exclusively with T-Series, Alka began receiving a wider variety of female playback assignments.

“Luckily, Anuradha Ji stopped singing for films and made herself exclusive to T-Series. This worked in Alka Ji’s favour, as she got both Lata Ji and Asha Ji type songs, whether they were solos, duets or shayari,” he said.

Taurani further recalled the scale of Alka Yagnik’s presence during the period, saying she was receiving a significant number of songs compared with some of the leading male playback singers of the time.

“The situation was such that, among Udit, Sanu and Sonu, Alka Ji was getting the most songs,” he added.

The conversation featured Ramesh and Kumar Taurani discussing their experiences in the Hindi music industry and the changes they witnessed during the rise of the 1990s playback generation. The episode is part of Komal Nahta’s Game Changers: The Music Series, which focuses on conversations with singers, composers and other figures associated with Indian film music.

title: Rian Mukherjee wins Best Child Actor at Los Angeles Film Awards 2026 for Hindi film Manzil

Debutant actor Rian Mukherjee wins the Best Child Actor Award at the prestigious Los Angeles Film Awards 2026 for his Hindi film Manzil. Directed by his father and National Award-winning filmmaker Ram Kamal Mukherjee, the lead actors of the film are Rituparna Sengupta, Sanjay Suri, and Abhishek Kumar. Produced under the banners of Dhanbad Talkies and Endeavour Films, the film follows the journey of a writer and a photographer who accidentally meet at a resort.

Rian plays the role of Aron, son of writer Ananya, played by Rituparna Sengupta, who becomes an integral part of the narrative through his presence. "I am delighted that the jury members felt Rian's performance was worth recognition," says his father and filmmaker Ram Kamal Mukherjee. "I think he is a gifted actor, as he never had any formal training, yet he faced the camera and knew his lines by heart," he added.

Rituparna Sengupta, who plays Rian's mother in the film, was thrilled as well. "I have literally seen him grow before my eyes. I still remember seeing Rian when he was born. Ram and Sarbani are like family, and when Ram decided to cast Rian as my son in the film, I knew he would leave an impact," added Rituparna, who also dons the hat of creative producer for the film. Produced by Rajesh Singh and Sharmistha Mukherjee, the film is currently making the rounds at festivals globally. "Rian is a promising actor from India. He competed with international child actors and emerged as a winner because of his natural screen presence and restrained voice modulation in the given space," added jury member and veteran actor Jean Vincentelli.

The first look at this film was exclusively showcased at an award ceremony in Mumbai, where Rian's screen presence was appreciated by prominent actors present at the ceremony.

Rian is the only Indian to win at LAFA 2026, while the other winners are Jingnu Ning, who won the Best Picture Award for his film A Palmful of Stars, and Phil Aman, who won the Best Actor trophy for Soundcheck. Nazakati Maihemuti bagged Best Actress for A Palmful Of Stars. "I am an accidental actor," says Rian Mukherjee. "I enjoy acting because that's the only time I get to see my Baba at work. title: Nana Patekar’s autopsy CONFIRMS heart attack caused by blood clot in left main coronary artery: Report
raw_summary:
Veteran actor Nana Patekar died of a heart attack caused by a blood clot blocking the left main coronary artery, his postmortem examination has confirmed. A senior doctor at Goa Medical College and Hospital shared the findings after the autopsy was conducted following the actor's death on October 8.

Nana Patekar was 75. He was declared dead at 5.10 am after doctors attempted to revive him through cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) for around 45 minutes. The actor was at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, when he reportedly fell unwell. Autopsy confirms cause of death According to a PTI report, the postmortem examination found that Nana suffered an acute heart attack after a blood clot blocked the left main coronary artery. The artery supplies blood to a significant portion of the heart.

The autopsy report recorded the cause of death as, “acute myocardial infarction due to left main coronary artery thrombosis secondary to atherosclerotic occlusive coronary artery disease, a natural cause of death”.

The findings establish that Nana's death was due to natural causes. Doctors had initially suspected a heart attack when the actor was brought to hospital, but the postmortem examination later provided the specific medical cause. Doctors attempted CPR for around 45 minutes Nana reportedly became unwell at his home in Dona Paula. His caretaker contacted a private hospital and requested an ambulance. Since the actor's residence was located less than a kilometre from the hospital, an ambulance was dispatched to the house.

Medical personnel reportedly began resuscitation efforts after reaching the residence. Doctors continued CPR for approximately 45 minutes but were unable to revive him.

Nana was subsequently declared dead at 5.10 am on October 8. His mortal remains were later taken to Goa Medical College and Hospital for the postmortem examination. Nana Patekar's mortal remains taken to Maharashtra Following the actor's death, his son Malhar Patekar travelled to Goa to bring his father's mortal remains back to Maharashtra.

The body was first taken to Pune and later transported to Nana's farmhouse in Donje village. The veteran actor was cremated there with full state honours.

Nana Patekar's death brought an end to a career spanning several decades across Hindi and Marathi cinema. Known for his intense performances and distinctive screen presence, the actor had continued to remain active in films until his final years.
